title: File:Central Idaho Debris Flow.jpg
description:
During August 2013, the Beaver Creek wildfire burned more than 114,000 acres in south-central Idaho. Shortly after the fire was contained, heavy rainfall triggered numerous debris flows, including this one in Badger Gulch. USGS hydrologists Dave Evetts (left) and Jake Jacobson examine the debris flow while in the burn area to install precipitation gages. The gages will be used to monitor rainfall that could trigger additional debris flows. 
Location: Hailey, ID, USA. Taken on 5/28/2014. Credit:

title: File:Earthflow (Canyon de Chelly National Monument, Arizona, USA) 1.jpg
description:
This dry creek is in Arizona's Canyon de Chelly National Monument.  The feature at center appears to be a type of landslide deposit, involving earth / soil / regolith that has moved as a viscous fluid.  Such landslides are called "earthflows".  The lobate-shaped landslide deposit diverted the original course of the stream.
Stratigraphy: De Chelly Sandstone, Leonardian Stage, Lower Permian

Locality: view from Mummy Cave overlook, "Canyon del Muerto" (= Canyon of the Dead), Canyon de Chelly Natio

title: File:Road cut fault - Red Rock Canyon.jpg
description: Pumice (Shoshone Ignimbrite/Resting Spring Tuff), erupted by a volcano during the Miocene epoch, seen in a roadcut on CA 178 near Shoshone, California, USA. Rocks at this location include devitrified pumice tuff, welded tuff and vesicular vitrophyre. The volcanic rocks are cut by faults. This road cut is known informally by geologists as "the Charlie Brown Outcrop" because the road is the Charles Brown Highway.
